findings.how_to_check: Across state files, run: count if namefrst!="" & namelast!="" & fs_namefrst!="" & fs_namelast!="" & !(namefrst==fs_namefrst & namelast==fs_namelast) & (namefrst_ml=="" | namelast_ml_ditto==""). Sum this count across all states to quantify omitted records. Add this total to Tdisc_s and Tnei_s to evaluate the impact on reported agreement rates.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the strict denominator using only the four human fields: namefrst!="" & namelast!="" & fs_namefrst!="" & fs_namelast!="" & !(namefrst==fs_namefrst & namelast==fs_namelast). Do not condition disc_s on namefrst_ml!="" & namelast_ml_ditto!="". Keep the model equality conditions as-is, and classify records where the model produces missing/empty output into nei_s (or report an explicit unread/omitted category).
findings.title: Strict variant conditions denominator on non-empty model output, dropping model transcription failures
findings.what_the_code_does: In lines 82-83, the strict denominator disc_s requires all six name fields to be non-empty: `namefrst!="" & namelast!="" & fs_namefrst!="" & fs_namelast!="" & namefrst_ml!="" & namelast_ml_ditto!="" & !(namefrst==fs_namefrst & namelast==fs_namelast)`. Any record where human transcribers provide complete names but the model outputs blank (e.g. segmentation failure or unreadable text) is dropped from disc_s rather than counted as a failure of the model to match humans in nei_s.
findings.why_it_matters: The paper reports these percentages as model agreement conditional on human transcribers disagreeing. Conditioning the denominator on non-empty model outputs creates survivorship/coverage selection bias by evaluating the model only on records it successfully transcribed. Because illegibility causing human disagreement also causes model transcription omission, dropping model blanks from the denominator shrinks disc_s and artificially inflates the headline agreement percentage (Tanc_s + Tfs_s)/Tdisc_s. Vacuous ""=="" agreement is fully prevented by requiring only the four human fields to be non-empty.

findings.how_to_check: Inspect the generated CSV file header and rows; confirm that columns disc, anc, fs, both, and nei correspond to the as-coded lines 61-77. Check downstream analysis scripts to verify whether they ingest the un-suffixed columns.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the CSV columns to distinguish the variants explicitly (e.g., disc_ascoded, anc_ascoded vs disc_strict, anc_strict) or write only the strict variant to the primary columns.
findings.title: CSV output writes vacuous-match-prone as-coded variant under primary column names
findings.what_the_code_does: The script computes the as-coded variant where `(namefrst!=""|namelast!="")` allows one name field to be blank, permitting vacuous agreement via Stata's `""==""` semantics. Although lines 19-22 document that the draft uses the strict variant and warn against publishing as-coded rates, lines 46, 97, and 119 write the as-coded metrics under the unqualified column names `disc,anc,fs,both,nei`, while the strict variant is relegated to `_s` suffixes.
findings.why_it_matters: Any downstream Stata script or analysis importing model_vs_human_discordant.csv referencing the default column names `disc, anc, fs` will ingest the counts contaminated by empty-string matches rather than the strict counts.

findings.how_to_check: Compare the display text at lines 128-129 and lines 138-139 against the count conditions at lines 67 and 88.

findings.title: Console display labels FamilySearch matches without the 'only' qualifier used for Ancestry
findings.what_the_code_does: Lines 128 and 138 print "matches Ancestry only   :", whereas lines 129 and 139 print "matches FamilySearch    :" without "only". Both counts (fs and fs_s) explicitly negate agreement with Ancestry in code.
findings.why_it_matters: The asymmetric labeling suggests FamilySearch agreement might be an inclusive or marginal share, whereas both categories are mutually exclusive source-only matches.

structured_output.summary: The script has successfully addressed earlier concerns regarding incomplete run assertions and geographic coverage documentation, and the strict partition logic is sound. However, the strict variant defines its discordant denominator by requiring both model fields to be non-empty alongside human fields, silently dropping model transcription failures rather than classifying them as non-matching. The single most important fix is to define the strict denominator over non-empty human transcriptions only, so model omission is properly penalized in the evaluation.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
